sources: [S3] Unbabel Danish Guidelines — 'du' is standard form
[S3] Microsoft Danish Localization Style Guide — informal 'du'
[S5] terms.json — Danish translations analyzed for consistency

falseFriends.performance: 'Ydeevne' = speed ratio in OEE, not general capability
falseFriends.station: Use 'arbejdsstation' for workstation; 'station' means train/bus/police station
falseFriends.scrap: Use 'spild' for quality rejects, not 'skrot' (metal recycling waste)
falseFriends.order: Use 'arbejdsordre' for production orders, not 'ordre' (commercial order)

grammarNotes.compoundWords: Danish forms compounds: 'cyklustid' (cycle time), 'nedetid' (downtime). Never split.
grammarNotes.enEt: Two genders with 'en' (common) and 'et' (neuter). Definite suffix: 'maskinen'/'skiftet'.
grammarNotes.softD: Danish pronunciation has swallowed consonants but writing is consistent.
grammarNotes.compoundPluralModifiers: Danish compound words inherently use singular modifier stems. Compound formation handles modifier singularity by construction. No compound pluralization issue.

industryContext.oeeTerminology: OEE acronym is used directly. Full Danish term: 'samlet udstyrseffektivitet'. No Danish equivalent of Swedish TAK.
industryContext.dominantSectors: Pharmaceuticals (Novo Nordisk), wind energy (Vestas), food (Danish Crown, Arla), pumps (Grundfos)

commonMistakes: Using 'De' instead of 'du' — 'De' is archaic in Danish; 'du' correct for all modern software
Splitting compound words: 'cykel tid' instead of 'cyklustid'
Using 'skrot' for production quality rejects instead of 'spild'
Wrong article (en vs et) for technical nouns
Using 'spild' ambiguously — in OEE context = quality rejects
notes: OEE is used; Danish workplace among most informal. 'du' is universal. P95 expansion 1.38x. Most compact Germanic language.
